review_notes: I read the whole file and compared it with the sibling ℕ/ℤ interface in Mathlib/Algebra/Module/NatInt.lean. I grepped for uses of the two cast-smul lemmas. The file has no simp or norm_cast attributes at all. I found no loops or competing rules. The one concern is a missing norm_cast attribute and the lack of a canonical simp direction for ℚ≥0/ℚ cast scalars. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether adding norm_cast would elaborate or behave well with the explicit R argument. I'm also unsure whether making the lemmas simp would be too aggressive, so I only propose norm_cast.

findings.excerpt:
lemma NNRat.cast_smul_eq_nnqsmul (R : Type*) [DivisionSemiring R]
    [MulAction R M] [MulAction ℚ≥0 M] [IsScalarTower ℚ≥0 R M]
    (q : ℚ≥0) (x : M) : (q : R) • x = q • x := by
findings.problem: The ℕ and ℤ analogues of these lemmas (`Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul`, `Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul`) are tagged `@[norm_cast]`. The ℚ≥0 and ℚ versions have no attribute, so the cast-scalar interface is inconsistent. Callers have to name the lemma and choose a direction by hand. Downstream files do this in both directions. Inner.lean and Average.lean use `simp [..., ← NNRat.cast_smul_eq_nnqsmul ℝ]`. RCLike/Basic.lean uses `simpa [NNRat.cast_smul_eq_nnqsmul]`. BaseExists.lean passes `Rat.cast_smul_eq_qsmul` to `simp` explicitly. This shows there is no canonical normal form for `(q : R) • x` versus `q • x`.
findings.proposed_change: Mirror the ℕ/ℤ lemmas and add `@[norm_cast]` to both lemmas. That gives `push_cast`/`norm_cast` a way to move between `(q : R) • x` and `q • x`. Whether to also make either a `simp` lemma is a separate decision. If not, document in the docstrings which direction callers should use. Then drop the explicit lemma arguments at the call sites where `norm_cast` or `push_cast` suffices.
findings.benefit: Users get the same cast-smul normalisation for ℚ≥0 and ℚ as for ℕ and ℤ, without remembering a lemma name and a rewrite direction at each call site. The downstream `simp [← ...]` and `simpa [...]` calls become uniform.
